report.measured_answer: 10 of 54 unique direct PyPI names publish platform-specific wheels (or sdist-only artifacts) on the current latest release: cryptography, numpy, onnxruntime, opencv-python-headless, pillow, playwright, pymupdf, pyside6, pyyaml, ruff. None of the declared names is sdist-only on PyPI today (sdist_only=[]). A local source-only C-extension control still reports compiler_required=true rather than a clean wheel pass. On the only measured declared target (Linux x86_64 / CPython 3.12.3) every declared name has a host-compatible wheel. Windows/macOS/ARM are packaging axes, not a found OS support matrix; packages whose latest wheels omit those axes: see fail_packaging_axes. AUD-0022 is absent, so this is not a full transitive closure. Probe 2 extracted host-compatible wheels into an isolated PYTHONPATH and attempted setuptools build_ext for the source-only control.
report.question_or_target: Which dependencies require a compiler, a platform-specific wheel, or a native runtime, and on which of the declared support platforms would each fail to install?
